section_1.title: The Flatland Foundation (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Establish prerequisite knowledge: Understand the N-1 rule. A 2D being (a square) can only see slices of a 3D object. Use a 2D grid to define the baseline of 'flat' perception.
section_1.example: A 2D 'Flatland' character, 'Flat-Fred,' encounters a 3D sphere passing through his plane, perceiving it only as a circle that grows and shrinks.

section_2.title: Projecting Higher Dimensions (0:45-2:00)
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of 'Dimensional Shadowing.' Explain how 3D objects are projected onto 2D screens and how 4D objects (tesseracts) would be projected into our 3D space.
section_2.example: Visualize a 3D wireframe cube casting a 2D square shadow on a wall. Then, animate a rotating 4D hypercube wireframe casting a complex 3D shadow.

section_3.title: Cross-Sectional Dynamics (2:00-3:30)
section_3.content: The 'Slice Method.' Demonstrate how moving an object through a lower-dimensional space reveals its internal structure. Focus on the mathematical correlation between rotation and slice area.
section_3.example: A 'Dimensional Slicer' device cuts a 3D cone at different angles; the audience observes the changing cross-sections (circle, ellipse, parabola) as the cone shifts position.

section_4.title: Unfolding the Impossible (3:30-4:30)
section_4.content: The 'Net' Strategy. Discuss how higher-dimensional objects can be 'unfolded' into lower dimensions to reveal their total structure, much like a 3D cardboard box flattened into 2D.
section_4.example: An animation showing a 3D cube unfolding into a 2D cross-shaped net, followed by the conceptual unfolding of a 4D tesseract into an 8-cube 'Dalí Cross' structure.

section_5.title: Synthesis and Summary (4:30-5:00)
section_5.content: Recap: Dimensional shifting is about mapping boundaries across N-1 spaces. Emphasize that 'seeing' higher dimensions requires logical inference rather than direct sight.
section_5.example: Final shot: A 3D robot arm manipulating a holographic 4D object, proving that even if we can't 'see' the 4th dimension, we can mathematically interact with it.
